airport.name: Lieutenant Colonel Luis A. Mantilla International Airport

summary: Lieutenant Colonel Luis A. Mantilla International Airport (TUA) serves Tulcán, the capital of Carchi Province in northern Ecuador, near the Colombian border. Situated high in the Andes at roughly 2,900 meters elevation, the airport provides an important gateway for travelers exploring the Ecuadorian-Colombian frontier region. It is named in honor of a distinguished Ecuadorian military aviator.
faqs:
Q: Where is Tulcán Airport located?
A: The airport is located in Tulcán, in Ecuador's northern Carchi Province, just a short distance from the Colombian border crossing at Ipiales.

Q: What is the elevation of the airport?
A: Tulcán sits high in the Andes Mountains, and the airport operates at an elevation of approximately 2,900 meters (9,500 feet) above sea level.

Q: Are there international flights from TUA?
A: The airport is classified as international and primarily handles domestic flights within Ecuador, with occasional regional charter operations.

Q: When is the best time to fly into Tulcán?
A: Morning flights are generally preferred because afternoon weather in the Andes can bring cloud cover and turbulence.
transport_tips: Taxis are the most common way to reach the airport from Tulcán's city center, typically a short 10-15 minute ride. Shared transport and shuttle services are also available, especially for travelers heading onward to the Colombian border. The airport has limited public transportation options, so arranging ground transport in advance is recommended.
local_tip: Bring layers of clothing — the high-altitude Andean location means temperatures can drop sharply after sunset, even in warmer months, and mornings at the airport can be quite chilly.
